title: A feast after the harvest
story: The rains have filled the fields and the granaries. The elders say a feast would honor the anito and show {neighbor} that this barangay prospers.

choices.label: A grand feast, with guests from {neighbor}
choices.result: Drums and songs carry across the water. The guests from {neighbor} go home full and talking of your generosity.

choices.label: A feast for our own families
choices.result: The barangay eats well for a night. Everyone works a little harder the next day.

choices.label: Save the rice
choices.result: The rice stays in the granary. The dry months will come soon enough.

_note: Competitive feasting was a central way for datus to show wealth and bind allies and followers.
sources: Laura Lee Junker, Raiding, Trading, and Feasting: The Political Economy of Philippine Chiefdoms (University of Hawai'i Press, 1999), on feasting and alliances
